assessment.summary: PolitiFact's independent replication and Bruenig's SCF-based analysis both show Bloomberg's ~$64.2B Forbes-estimated net worth (Feb 2020) far exceeds the ~$6-11.4B held by the bottom 38% of households (~125.7M people), supporting the claim.

evidence.finding: An independent analyst (Gross, via PolitiFact) replicated the math and found the bottom 38% of households held about $6 billion (vs Bruenig's $11.4 billion), verifying Bloomberg's wealth exceeded the bottom 38% combined either way.
Forbes estimated Bloomberg's net worth at $64.2 billion on Feb 19, 2020.
The bottom 38% of households (~47.8M households x 2.63 members ≈ 125.7M people) held ~$11.4 billion collective net worth per the 2016 SCF, so Bloomberg's wealth is nearly 6x greater.
The distributional comparison rests on the Federal Reserve's triennial Survey of Consumer Finances; the 2016 edition covering 2013-2016 was the underlying data source.

assertions.assertion: Former mayor of New York, US, Mike Bloomberg owns more wealth than the bottom 125 million Americans.

gaps: Distribution data is the 2016 SCF (latest available at runtime) mixed with a Feb 2020 Forbes net worth estimate; no 2019/2020 distribution data existed then (2019 SCF released Sept 2020, S12).
PolitiFact's fact-check was published 2020-03-02, after the 2020-02-19 runtime date, though it uses data contemporaneous with the debate.
The 'bottom 125 million' derives from an approximate household-to-person conversion (2.63 members/household ≈ 125.7M people).
